roster.note: 36m cut to 0: record margin debt, record equity allocations and index concentration are her stated longer-term risks

roster.name: Druckenmiller
roster.note: GAP WIDENED, not closed: still positioned long megacap tech from Q2, while publicly arguing rates are too LOW and yield suppression is a subsidy to fiscal procrastination. Bearish bonds, long equities, hawkish Fed - pick two
roster.statement_summary: Says rates are already too low and cuts are unnecessary - 'committee members on the Fed who keep saying Fed fund rates are restrictive are just ridiculous'; WSJ op-ed against Treasury long-bond buybacks: if the 30y must trade at 5.5% 'that isn't a crisis, it is an invoice', and the only durable fix is the primary deficit

roster.name: Roubini
roster.note: Held: benign baseline, tail risks judged less likely; nothing US-equity specific in the visible text
roster.statement_summary: Project Syndicate 'Why Is the Global Economy So Resilient?': markets and economy held up despite tariffs and the energy shock; growth improves in 2027

roster.name: Slok
roster.note: Held: near-term rates may peak on oil relief, but AI capex ignores higher rates so the Fed stays higher for longer; flags AI-company CDS widening
roster.statement_summary: Daily Spark: 'AI's Insensitivity to Interest Rates Is a Problem for the Fed' - 'the Fed will have to keep interest rates higher for longer' (follows 10-06 'Are Rates Peaking Within the Next Month?')

roster.name: El-Erian
roster.note: CALLED IT: in August he said the Treasury buyback was financial engineering that left long rates untouched. The 10y then went through 5%. His new line - interest-rate risk becoming equity and credit risk - is precisely what the HY tile is now showing
roster.statement_summary: Expects the 10y to stay around 5% even if oil falls, citing a structural bond supply/demand imbalance; 'volatility will be a feature, and elevated yields will be a feature for the rest of the year', and 'the big danger' is rate risk turning into equity and credit risk

roster.name: Gross
roster.note: MOVED CAUTIOUS from neutral: own nothing but 1-year T-bills, be cautious on stocks at record levels because higher yields will compress margins. FT is paywalled; quotes via secondary coverage, op-ed likely ran 09-30
roster.statement_summary: FT op-ed: 'don't own bonds, with the exception of one-year Treasury bills'; 'be cautious with stocks at record levels as higher yields over time will contract profit margins'

roster.name: Buffett-Berkshire
roster.note: Held: still a net buyer - ~2.4M Lennar A shares (~$190M) bought into homebuilder weakness on 10-01/02. Small next to $365bn cash, but buying housing exactly where Burry is shorting

roster.name: Marks
roster.note: No new memo inside the fortnight, but his private-credit memo is the live thesis: the US private-credit default rate hit a record 6.0% in April (Fitch) and the Proskauer index ran 2.73% in Q1 against 1.84% two quarters earlier - while loan spreads were still tightening. Exactly the 'not being paid for the risk' setup he described
roster.statement_summary: Memo 'What's Going On in Private Credit?' - direct lending's growth, and the issues rapid deployment created

roster.name: Dimon
roster.note: Held: the warning is now explicitly about credit spreads on refinancing - the HY tripwire in his own words. JPM Q3 earnings call mid-October is the next read
roster.statement_summary: Bloomberg interview in London: global demand for capital means 'the market will ask for more'; are refinancing borrowers 'prepared for higher credit spreads or not?'

roster.name: Krugman
roster.note: Held: AI capex is pushing rates up and crowding out everything else; flags private-credit and CRE spillover; no explicit index call
roster.statement_summary: Substack 'AI Versus Everything Else': hyperscaler boom is driving up interest rates and crowding out non-AI investment 'right now'

roster.name: Dalio
roster.note: Held at maximum conviction: 'we are in a bond bear market', AI a classic bubble near bursting, equities' cushion against yields shrinking - but declines to call an imminent selloff
roster.statement_summary: CNBC at Milken Asia (Singapore): stocks' buffer against rising bond yields is shrinking, credit spreads starting to widen, watch weakening free cash flow

roster.name: Rosenberg
roster.note: conviction up: says credit markets are already writing the warning - directly relevant to the HY tripwire
roster.statement_summary: With Richard Bernstein: the AI trade is a bubble, real disposable income is fractionally negative y/y, and ex-AI the four-quarter real GDP trend is under 1.5% - a K-shaped economy where profits take all the income growth

roster.name: Grantham
roster.note: latest sourced statement is June 2026 - inside the 6-month window but not fresh this fortnight
roster.statement_summary: Calls this 'the most expensive market in American history'; a reversion to trend would be closer to a wipeout than a correction, and the odds an AI bubble does not bust are 'slim to none'

roster.name: Burry
roster.note: Held. GAP flagged the other way: rhetoric is maximal but no verifiable current positioning (Scion deregistered 2025), so the scores rest on talk. Market in the 'denial' stage that lasted 6-9 months in 2000/2008
roster.statement_summary: X posts: homebuilders' 'salad days won't last', Fannie/Freddie 'head-and-shoulders top' with heavy dilution risk; ~10-06 'first stage of grief, denial'
